messages:
alex.dev: Hey team, hit a weird one — customer reported a sudden short spike (~5x) for ~30s that exhausted their per-minute quota and the burst credits didn't seem to kick in. They say tokens kept getting 429s even after the spike subsided. Anyone seen this pattern?
priya_support: Thanks for flagging, alex. Do we have the request IDs or customer org id? Also which quota (per-minute or per-second) and are they on smoothing enabled plan?
alex.dev: Org org-8245. Request IDs: r-94a1, r-94a2, r-94a3. They were on default hosted quota + burst credits (no custom smoothing config). Per-minute token quota was 1,000, per-second was 50. Spike was ~250 req/s for 20-30s, avg token size ~300.
manuel_infra: Quick theory: burst credits are consumed from a token-bucket-like pool with a refill interval. If credits were already low and refill cadence hadn't topped up yet, sustained spike can exhaust them and subsequent checks fallback to strict quota until refill. Need to check the bucket state and server-side logs.
joy_product: Timeline question — did the 429s persist for >1 minute after the spike? That helps distinguish between bucket exhaustion vs. an enforcement bug.
alex.dev: They reported 429s for ~40s after the spike ended. So yes, a little after.
priya_support: Pulling logs now. @ratebot can you fetch rate-limiter trace for org-8245 around 1977777700-1977777860?
ratebot: Fetching traces for org-8245 — matched 14 entries. Attached snippets below.
ratebot: "[rate-check] ts=1977777723 org=org-8245 req=r-94a1 token_bucket_remaining=0 burst_credits=0 enforcement=ENFORCE"
ratebot: "[refill] ts=1977777800 org=org-8245 refill_amount=200 burst_credits_post=200"
manuel_infra: Looks like burst_credits hit 0 at 1977777723 and didn't refill until 1977777800 — 77s gap. That's longer than usual. Refill cadence should be ~60s. Need to check the scheduler.
emma_sre: I see a correlated cron backoff on the refill job in that region due to a transient DB lock (node-3). The job retried with exponential backoff, which pushed the refill past the nominal window.
joy_product: That explains the delay. But question: even if refill delayed, why did the enforcement persist after refill started for some requests? Any cache or eventual consistency?
manuel_infra: Our enforcement checks the in-memory bucket on every request; refill writes go to central store then propagate. If a request hits a different serving node before refill propagation, it can still see 0. We try to keep propagation under a few seconds, but with the DB lock & retry the window got messy.
priya_support: For the customer: are there recommended mitigations we can advise? Suggest immediate fixes + longer-term config changes?
joy_product: Short-term: suggest enabling smoothing (burst_smoothing) for their API key which enforces a decaying smoothing window so short spikes are averaged before enforcement. Also suggest increasing per-second quota temporarily or preloading credits if they expect a burst. Long-term: adjust refill health checks + region failover.
alex.dev: Can we confirm exact smoothing config knobs? Customer asked for recommended numbers.
manuel_infra: Current smoothing implementation accepts two params: smoothing_window_seconds (default 30) and smoothing_rate (tokens/sec allowed under smoothing). For their use case (300 tokens/request, short spike 20-30s), I’d recommend smoothing_window_seconds=60 and smoothing_rate=800/sec combined with an increased per-second quota to 200 during the rollout. That should absorb 30s surges.
priya_support: I messaged the customer with those config values and asked if they want us to apply temporarily. They also asked for repro steps so they can test.
emma_sre: Repro steps we used in staging:
```
# hammer for 30s at ~250 req/s with 300 tokens
wrk -t50 -c250 -d30s --script=post.lua https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# monitor rate-check logs on serving nodes
kubectl logs -l app=rate-limiter -f
```
manuel_infra: Also include snippet to read burst credits endpoint: GET /v1/orgs/{org}/burst-credits -> returns {"remaining": 120, "refill_at": 1977777860} (in prod it's behind auth).
joy_product: One more operational tip: enable proactive refill alerts when refill job latency > 5s or when credits fall below 20% so SRE can intervene before user-visible 429s.
priya_support: Customer accepted temporary smoothing and slight quota bump. I applied smoothing_window_seconds=60 smoothing_rate=800 and bumped per-second to 200 for org-8245 at 1977777825.
ratebot: Config change applied by priya_support (uid-priya) at 1977777826.
alex.dev: After change, customer reported failed calls dropped to zero and token bucket shows remaining=150 by 1977777840. Nice.
priya_support: Leaving note on the ticket: root cause = transient refill job delay combined with exhausted burst credits. Remediation = applied smoothing + quota bump; SRE to patch refill job retry behavior.
emma_sre: Filed infra incident INF-2026-72: Adjust refill job retry backoff and improve monitoring.
joy_product: I'll add an entry to docs: tips for configuring smoothing and burst expectations (include default values + recommended patterns).
alex.dev: Thanks all. For internal follow-up, can we get a one-paragraph explanation I can paste into the customer's postmortem?
manuel_infra: "Customer spike exhausted burst credits. Refill job delayed due to DB lock retries; propagation lag caused additional enforcement on some nodes. We applied smoothing_window_seconds=60 and smoothing_rate=800 plus a temporary per-second quota increase to 200. SRE will change refill job retry behavior and add refill-latency alerts."
priya_support: Pasting that into the ticket now. Customer replied :thumbsup: and asked for doc link. joy_product, can you attach once live?
joy_product: Will do, ETA 24h. Adding to docs backlog with link once published. :white_check_mark:
